actions.text: Preserve the official accounting label exactly enough to prevent a different measure being substituted.
Check geographic/accounting boundary before comparing or joining the value.
Record the stated estimation method or proxy before promotion.
Record publication year/version and reject silent cross-year factor substitution.
Attach the official source URL and publisher to the derived control.
Expose material limitations or provisional status in the web row.
Block year-on-year or cross-source comparison when methods are not comparable.
Do not convert national/organisational methodology into a measured parcel emission value.
Fail closed when required source metadata are absent.
Require review when the source explicitly warns about revisions, proxy use, or other-use risk.

sources.title: Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Conversion factors 2026: statement of voluntary compliance with the Code of Practice for Statistics

facts.text: 2026 factors calculate and report emissions from UK activities using activity data such as fuel volume, purchased electricity kWh or distance travelled.
The 2026 factors support separate reporting of Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions.
The factors are suitable for UK-based organisations of all sizes and international organisations reporting UK operations.
The factors are relevant to Environmental Reporting Guidelines including Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting.
The factors may be used for other purposes, but GOV.UK states users do so at their own risk.
The factors are updated annually, with a methodology report and a major-changes report.
The DESNZ activity-based conversion factors differ from Defra spend-based emissions multipliers.
Spend-based methods can provide an initial supply-chain assessment where sufficient activity data are unavailable.
Users should report the methods used for emissions accounting.
New users should read the Introduction guidance/FAQs and worksheet-specific guidance in the full set.
Regular users should review the What’s new worksheet to support consistent and comparable year-on-year reporting.
A flat-file spreadsheet is explicitly provided for automatic processing.
A full-set spreadsheet is provided for all users.
A dedicated methodology document accompanies the 2026 factors.
A dedicated major-changes document accompanies the 2026 factors.

PROVISIONAL_2025_ESTIMATION_RELIABILITY.title: 2025 provisional GHG estimation and reliability controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: 2025 UK greenhouse gas emissions: provisional figures - methodology summary

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: 2025 UK greenhouse gas emissions: provisional figures - statistical release

facts.text: Provisional estimates use four methodological categories: energy-derived, energy-held-constant, non-energy-projection-derived and non-energy-held-constant.
About 77% of total GHG emissions in the 2024 final statistics are represented by provisional estimates derived from energy-use data.
Energy-derived provisional estimates assume the year-on-year percentage change in emissions follows the corresponding energy-use change.
Energy scaling factors are produced across 29 category/fuel groups.
A small set of energy-use emissions is held constant where Energy Trends has no suitable scaling data.
Most non-energy provisional emissions are derived from the latest Energy and Emissions Projections reference-scenario growth factors.
Agriculture, waste, LULUCF and other buildings/product uses are largely projection-derived and are marked as estimates in published tables.
Some non-energy emissions are held constant because proxy projections do not separate them from energy-use emissions.
Historically the provisional year-on-year total change has usually been within one percentage point of the later final estimate, but revisions still occur.
Temperature-adjusted estimates remove the effect of external-temperature differences from selected energy-use emissions.
Temperature adjustment uses heating degree days relative to a long-term average.
Temperature adjustment is applied only where regression evidence shows a statistically significant temperature relationship and sufficiently strong R-squared.
The current long-term average for temperature adjustment is 1991-2020.
International aviation and shipping bunker emissions are reported separately as memo items and are not included in the UK territorial total.
Provisional international aviation/shipping emissions use Energy Trends fuel proxies; lubricant-related aviation emissions are held constant.
Quarterly and temperature-adjusted estimates are not produced for international aviation and shipping bunker emissions.
Provisional methodologies are periodically updated as understanding and data improve.
For 2025, non-renewable municipal solid waste use in power stations was updated to use provisional energy-balance data instead of simply holding emissions constant.
2025 values remain provisional and are due to be replaced by final estimates in February 2027.
The provisional publication is territorial and by-source: emissions are attributed to the sector that emits them directly.

FINAL_2024_REVISION_BOUNDARY.title: 2024 final GHG revision and accounting-boundary controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Final UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics: 1990 to 2024

facts.text: Final 1990-2024 estimates revise the full time series to incorporate methodological improvements and new data, superseding previous estimates.
Final estimates are presented by source in February, updated in March for end-user estimates and in June for SIC estimates.
Territorial statistics cover emissions occurring within UK borders.
On a source basis, emissions are attributed to the sector that emits them directly.
On an end-user basis, energy-supply emissions are modelled and reallocated to where the energy is ultimately used.
DESNZ territorial statistics do not estimate overseas emissions associated with UK consumption.
Territorial Emissions Statistics use broad sectors including electricity supply, fuel supply, domestic transport, buildings/product uses, industry, agriculture, waste and LULUCF.
Detailed sectors follow IPCC definitions used in UNFCCC reporting.
ONS distinguishes territorial, residence/production and footprint/consumption measures.
Territorial estimates include emissions from activities within UK borders, including UK businesses regardless of registration, residents/visitors, and UK land.
Territorial estimates currently exclude international aviation/shipping, UK residents/businesses abroad, and imported-production emissions.
Residence emissions cover UK residents and UK-registered businesses whether emissions occur in the UK or overseas.
Footprint emissions cover supply-chain emissions for goods/services consumed in the UK wherever produced, include imports and exclude exported UK production.
ONS states the residence measure covers Scope 1 direct emissions.
ONS states the footprint measure covers Scopes 1, 2 and 3.
ONS states all three measures report using AR5 global warming potentials aligned with international reporting practice.
ONS notes historical estimates are revised each year due to underlying data revisions or methodological improvements.
The three measures answer different accounting questions and should not be substituted without preserving their boundary definitions.
